finding.http_versions.no_http2: The HTTPS server does not offer HTTP/2 (HTTP/1.1 only): probably outdated server software.
http_versions.score_no_https: HTTPS unavailable: HTTP versions not applicable
module.http_versions.checks: Detects HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support (ALPN negotiation) and HTTP/3 advertisement (Alt-Svc header, HTTPS DNS record).
module.http_versions.fix:
Identify which software terminates HTTPS (nginx, Apache, IIS, Caddy, load balancer or CDN) and its version, for example with `nginx -v` or `apachectl -v`. HTTP/2 needs nginx 1.9.5 or later, Apache 2.4.17 or later with `mod_http2`, or IIS 10 (Windows Server 2016 or later): below that, update the software.
Enable HTTP/2 on the HTTPS listener (see the snippet). IIS 10 and Caddy turn it on by themselves as soon as a site is served over HTTPS; behind a CDN or a load balancer, enable it in its network settings.
Check that the server accepts TLS 1.2 or later with modern cipher suites: HTTP/2 is not negotiated below TLS 1.2.
For HTTP/3 (optional, recommended): open UDP port 443 in the firewall and at the host, enable QUIC on the server (nginx 1.25.0 or later built with the HTTP/3 module; Caddy does it by default) or at the CDN, then advertise HTTP/3 with the `Alt-Svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400` header or with an HTTPS-type DNS record (nginx HTTP/3 and DNS snippets).
If the server stays limited to HTTP/1.1 because the software is old or runs on an unmaintained system, plan its update or replacement: it is often the sign of a component that no longer receives fixes.
Check: `curl -sI --http2 https://example.com | head -1` must show `HTTP/2 200` (or the page's status code); on Linux, `openssl s_client -alpn h2 -connect example.com:443 < /dev/null` must contain `ALPN protocol: h2`; for HTTP/3, `curl -sI https://example.com | grep -i alt-svc` must show `h3`. Then run the scan again.
module.http_versions.title: HTTP versions
module.http_versions.why: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 speed up the site and reduce the attack surface of older protocols. A server limited to HTTP/1.1 is often ageing software.
